subject: Dedicated capacity baseline & proposed next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity baseline & proposed next steps

Hi Lydia — thanks again for a focused conversation this morning. Quick recap and a concrete set of next steps so we can keep momentum toward a pilots / reserved capacity commitment.

Summary of customer needs (as heard):
- Workload: real-time clinical inference (PHI) with occasional batch scoring for model retraining.
- Throughput target: ~2M tokens/day average, with predictable peaks up to ~400 concurrent inference requests during rollout windows.
- Isolation/security: VPC-private control plane, SOC2 and FIPS-compliant options required; HSM/KMS for key material; audit logs retained 13 months.
- Latency SLO: p95 end-to-end generation <150ms for short prompts (<256 tokens); steady-state p50 ~40–60ms desired.
- Reliability: 99.9% uptime target for inference endpoints; need an escalation path and playbook for incidents that impact latency or availability.

Initial recommendation (the short version):
- Dedicated pool: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (quarter-node sizing) reserved with a burst capacity policy to +4 GPUs for scheduled batch windows. This balances steady-state cost predictability and headroom for retrains/batches.
- Isolation: single-tenant pool in Aurelia's selected cloud region with VPC peering and private networking (we'll provide a connectivity checklist).
- Model variants: start with a quantized MPT-30B variant (best guess) and a fallback Llama-2-70B float32 variant for complex prompts. We will provide latency and throughput estimates after a 48-hour micro-benchmark using your sample prompt set.
- Autoscaling & routing: policy-driven autoscaler with hard cap at reserved capacity and controlled burst behavior; route 90% of traffic to the dedicated pool and keep a small cross-region fallback in case of saturation.
- Cost controls: intelligent KV-caching and batching to keep per-token costs low; we'll surface expected unit economics for both Live and Batch usage.

Action items & timeline:
1) Rishi -> send connectivity & compliance questionnaire (attached) and draft SLA term sheet (attached) — done (see attachments).
2) Lydia -> confirm list of sample prompts and a 24–48 hour window when your infra team can provide network access for benchmarking (target: within 5 business days).
3) Ben -> run a preliminary capacity estimate and perf model based on the prompt set once provided; propose 2 benchmark configurations (4x and 8x GPU).
4) Marissa -> capture commercial path (recommended committed run-rate, discount tranche, procurement checklist) and share draft SOW after Ben's perf numbers.

Questions / clarifications from our side:
- Can you confirm whether Aurelia will require FedRAMP/FIPS at contract signature or only for production cutover?
- Are there restrictions on external egress that would prevent our telemetry/tracing hooks (we can do ephemeral telemetry if needed)?

Suggested next touchpoints: 1) Perf window (48 hrs) scheduled next week; 2) Internal readiness call with Aurelia infra + Redwood ops (30m) the day after perf window.

If this reads accurately, I'll queue Ben to plan the perf tests and Marissa to draft a commercial outline.

Thanks — Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra

From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@aureliahealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@aureliahealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 13:02:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity baseline & proposed next steps

Hi Rishi — thanks for the clear recap. This matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from Aurelia's side before we schedule the perf window: 

1) Security/regulatory: We need production-grade FIPS support and an HSM-backed KMS at go-live. For the pilot we can accept KMS only, but FedRAMP is out of scope for now.

2) Data residency: All inference must run in our primary US-east region; secondary region for fallback is acceptable so long as data does not transit outside the US without prior approval.

3) Bench items: I'll attach the sample prompt set and a short lookup table with expected token distributions. We can open a perf window next Thursday (9 Dec) morning (US/PST). Is that still workable on your side?

4) Commercial: procurement would like a simple itemized cost sheet for the reserved pool (monthly committed cost), an overage rate for burst, and an estimated unit cost per 1k tokens for the two model configurations you recommended. Can you send that to procurement@aureliahealth.com and me?

Finally, we are highly sensitive to initial latency and need to see p95 numbers for short prompts below 150ms. If you can commit to that level in the pilot configuration that will be a strong signal for our execs.

Thanks — Lydia

Lydia Park
VP, AI Platforms | Aurelia Health
lydia.park@aureliahealth.com | (212) 555-0129

I've attached the questionnaire and draft SLA we already shared with Aurelia. Let's keep the first draft reply to procurement under 48 hours so we can lock a perf window. If you want, I can join the bench setup call with OE (ops eng).

Thanks — Rishi
